edges.description: The barrier breach delivers enteric aerobic and anaerobic organisms into peritoneal fluid and onto mesothelial surfaces.
Bacterial products contact mesothelial and resident innate immune cells, which respond by releasing inflammatory mediators.
Mesothelial cytokine and chemokine release promotes recruitment of neutrophils into the peritoneal cavity.
Peritoneal innate immune activation can spread systemically as a dysregulated host response with organ dysfunction.
Peritonitis favors peritoneal coagulation and impaired fibrin clearance, promoting loculated abscess formation.
Uncontrolled local bacterial infection can spread into a systemic septic host response.
Peritoneal irritation produces the abdominal pain and tenderness of an acute abdomen.
Purulent peritoneal inflammation impairs bowel motility and produces diminished or absent bowel sounds.
Peritoneal inflammation irritates the abdominal cavity and produces local guarding or rigidity.
Peritoneal inflammation produces distention and diminished bowel sounds as acute-abdomen manifestations.
Local peritoneal infection drives systemic inflammatory signs including fever.
Local peritoneal infection can progress to systemic inflammation with tachycardia.
Acute perforation peritonitis can present with dehydration during the systemic inflammatory acute-abdomen syndrome.
intermediate_mechanisms: Third spacing and systemic inflammatory response

edges.description: Intra-abdominal infection can drive the dysregulated systemic host response and organ dysfunction that define sepsis.

edges.limitations: The devitalized cecum remains in place, so CLP does not model an episode where surgical source control closes or removes the leaking focus.

evidence.snippet: The aim of source control is to reduce microbial load by removing the infection source and it is achievable by using a wide range of procedures, such as definitive surgical removal of anatomic infectious foci, percutaneous drainage and toilette of infected collections, decompression, and debridement of infected and necrotic tissue or device removal
